title: Using Tomoauto: A Protocol for High-throughput Automated Cryo-electron Tomography
protocol: Transform 1 µl of plasmid pBS58 into 5 µl electrocompetent Streptomycin-resistant serotype 5a (M90T-Sm) cells by electroporation at 2.5 kV for 5 msec in 1 mm cuvettes.
Store minicell samples at -80 °C in 15% glycerol in a 1.5 ml cryogenic microtube.
Scrape approximately 5 μl of cells from the unthawed microtube using a pipette tip and suspend the cells in 4 ml tryptic soy broth with spectinomycin added to 100 μg/ml concentration.
Grow O/N at 37 °C.
Pipette 2 ml of the culture into 200 ml tryptic soy broth with spectinomycin again added to 100 μg/ml concentrations.
Grow at 37 °C to late log phase.
Centrifuge 200 ml of the culture at 1,000 x g for 5 min.
Carefully pour the supernatant fraction into a new centrifuge tube and centrifuge at 20,000 x g for 10 min.
Carefully pour off and discard the supernatant fraction.
Gently mix the pellet with the remaining liquid using a pipette tip.
Transfer approximately 100 μl of the pellet mixture to a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Place a R2/2 holey carbon film 200-mesh copper grid carbon side up on a glass slide.
Place the slide on the platform in a glow discharge device.
Power on the probe for 1 min to glow discharge the grid.
Remove the grid with a set of forceps.
Lock the forceps closed with an elastic band.
Add 100 μl of 10 nm colloidal gold solution to the microcentrifuge tube containing the minicells and mix by gently flicking the tube.
Place 4 μl of the mixture on the grid.
Prepare the plunge-freeze apparatus by filling the outer freezing container with liquid nitrogen and then filling the inner chamber with liquid ethane.
Attach the forceps with the grid to the plunger rod and lock the plunger rod into the raised position.

Blot the grid by carefully touching a piece of filter paper to the drop of sample until the meniscus between the grid and filter paper separates and the wicking on the filter paper stops, then immediately release the plunger rod, freezing the grid.
Carefully remove the forceps from the plunger rod.
Place the grid into a grid holder.
Prepare the cryo-EM transfer station by filling the loading area and absorption pump container with liquid nitrogen.
Place the grid holder and a microscope specimen cartridge in the loading area once cooled to liquid nitrogen temperature.
Remove the lock ring from the cartridge; place the EM grid into the cartridge using forceps.
Gently reattach the lock ring back onto the cartridge securing the grid.
Remove the multiple specimen holder from the microscope and attach it to the transfer station.
Place the specimen cartridge into the holder using cartridge forceps.
Retract the holder from the loading area.
Transfer the multiple specimen holder back to the microscope.
Adjust the stage to eucentric height by tilting the specimen holder to 50°.
Adjust the z-height until the x-y translation of the stage is minimal between the tilted and untilted views.
Move to the center of the grid square.
Click the 'Add Stage Pos' button in the Navigator window to store the current stage position.
Open a new montage MRC file by clicking 'New montage' in the 'File' menu.
In the Montage Setup Dialog, select a number of pieces in X and Y that will acquire the entire grid square (e.g., 10 x 10 for a standard 200 mesh grid).
Use a high binning such as 8.
Select the 'Move Stage Instead of Shifting Image' radio button.
Select the 'Skip correlations used to align pieces' radio button.
Click the first stage position in the Navigator window and set it to be acquired by checking the 'Acquire' checkbox.
Repeat this for each stage position in the Navigator window.
Open the Navigator Acquire Dialog by clicking 'Acquire at Points' in the 'Navigator' menu.
Check the 'Acquire map image' checkbox.
Check the 'Rough eucentricity' checkbox.
Make sure that all other checkboxes are unchecked.
Click 'Proceed' to collect a montage at each stage position.
Click the 'Add Points' button in the Navigator window and select points for acquiring a tilt-series in the map.
Click the 'Stop Adding Points' button when finished adding points.
Repeat steps 1-2 for each map collected.
In the Camera menu, select 'Parameters' to define Focus, Trial, and Record mode parameters.
Select a point in the Navigator window and check the 'Tilt-Series' checkbox.
Open the Tilt-Series Setup dialog window and set desired collection parameters.
Repeat step 5 for all selected points but do not select maps.
In the Navigator menu, select 'Acquire at Points'.
Choose 'Realign to item', Autofocus', and 'Rough eucentricity' as Preliminary tasks in the Navigator Acquire dialog.
Select 'Acquire tilt series' as the Primary task.
Check 'Close column valves at end' to close the column when all points are collected.
Proceed with data collection for a tilt-series at each point in each map.
In a terminal, execute the command dose_fractioned_to_stack <filename.st>.
With the tilt-series in the current working directory, in a terminal execute the command tomoauto --CTF --mode=align <filename.st> <fid_diam>.
Execute the command `tomoauto --CTF <filename.st> <fid_diam>` for automatic alignment and CTF estimation of the tilt-series.
Inspect the aligned tilt-series visually using `3dmod <filename>.ali`.
Inspect the estimated CTF by executing `submfg <filename>_ctfplotter.com`.
Check the output of the tomoauto command for mean residual error statistics.
Proceed with reconstruction if alignment quality is acceptable, using `tomoauto --CTF --mode=reconstruct <filename.st> <fid_diam>` command.
Open the reconstructed tomogram for particle picking by executing the command: tomopick <filename>.rec
Select injectisomes using the left mouse button in the tomogram viewer, clicking first on the basal body and then on the needle tip.
Use up and down arrow keys to navigate through the slices of the tomogram.
Store coordinates in a text file defining the long axis of the structure and estimating two Euler angles describing the orientation.
Execute the command: clip resize -cx <x> -cy <y> -cz <z> -ix 400 -iy 400 -iz 400 to extract 4003 voxel cubes centered at the midpoint of the defined long axis.
Extract a cube from the structure using midpoint coordinates and appropriate size.
Down-sample (bin) the sub-tomogram by a factor of four.
Apply determined Euler angles to sub-tomograms.
Compute the global average to produce the initial template.
Align and classify down-sampled sub-tomograms using a binary classification mask.
Perform sub-tomogram averaging in Fourier space for binning 4 data with SAMPFACT="4 4 4".
Repeat step using sub-tomograms down-sampled by a factor of two (SAMPFACT="2 2 2").
Repeat step once more with the original data (SAMPFACT="1 1 1").
